accounts.prose: Executes synchronous or asynchronous callbacks behind policy-supplied error/result predicates, classifies their outcomes, and exposes timed success/failure notifications. It also provides the small adapter that turns classified outcomes back into ordinary return-or-throw behavior.

referent.description: Executor module and its exported execution/outcome API

qualifications: Interpretation of first-observed TypeScript source; source establishes implementation text, not executed behavior in a particular runtime.
Configured-project module/dependency analysis is bounded and does not establish runtime dependency completeness.

accounts.prose: `FailureOrSuccess<R>` distinguishes ordinary success from policy-handled error or value failures. `returnOrThrow` throws the error case and returns either the success or handled value case.

referent.description: Classified outcome union and its unwrapping adapter

qualifications: The three cases are structurally discriminated by property presence; malformed external values are outside the declared type contract.

associations.subject: session:0433ea25-913d-4dc3-a8e5-084e76f8b207:module:34b0c70333c5c2ef743310876c47d82311b0793d606dafb59fa24640c304352c
qualifications: FailureReason contributes the `{error}` and `{value}` branches; Executor adds `{success}`.

accounts.prose: `invoke` awaits the callback. An unfiltered value becomes `{success}`; a filtered value becomes handled `{value}`. A filtered exception becomes `{error}`; an unfiltered exception is rethrown after failure notification. Timing is skipped unless a success or failure listener exists, using `performance.now()` when available and `process.hrtime.bigint()` otherwise.

referent.description: ExecuteWrapper invocation, filtering, timing, and notification mechanism

qualifications: Behavior is inferred from the captured implementation; platform availability and timing precision were not executed or tested.

qualifications: EventEmitter.size gates stopwatch creation; addListener and emit implement the notification channel.

accounts.prose: `clone` preserves both predicates but creates fresh emitters, so derived policy instances share classification rules rather than subscriptions.
qualifications: Fresh-listener behavior follows from construction of a new wrapper and per-instance emitter fields.
